elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase commitment.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Customer commits to purchase “no minimum amount of Services.”

elements.element: Customer pays fees only for Services it orders or uses.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that Customer “pays only for Services ordered or used.”

elements.element: Any Customer minimum purchase commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: No enforceable minimum purchase commitment exists, so the duration condition is inapplicable notwithstanding the unnecessary reference to the next three years.

elements.element: Customer may reduce any minimum purchase commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: There is no minimum commitment to reduce, and the clause is more permissive because it expressly imposes no reduction restrictions.

elements.element: Any shortfall against a minimum purchase commitment is reconciled through a true-up.
elements.evidence: Because the clause creates no minimum commitment, no shortfall can arise and the true-up condition is not triggered.

elements.element: No penalty applies to a shortfall against or reduction of a minimum purchase commitment.
elements.evidence: The clause rejects take-or-pay treatment and requires payment only for Services ordered or used, leaving no penalty for a commitment shortfall.

result.reason: The operative language fully reaches the preferred no-minimum, usage-or-order-based position. It also satisfies the fallback protections because there is no minimum commitment or shortfall to which its duration and true-up conditions could apply, while reduction is unrestricted and take-or-pay is removed. The redline is not minimal and may disturb unrelated termination terms: replacing the original limitation with “without ... termination restrictions” is broader than necessary and could be read to create unrestricted termination rights. Drafting is also awkward because a commitment to purchase “no minimum amount” over each of three years is conceptually unnecessary.
